title: battery applet should not report that the power supply is not powerful enough to charge battery when it is above the stop charge limit
line: When a plugged-in laptop is discharging because the battery is above its charge limit, the battery tooltip now shows the charge limit instead of saying the power supply is too weak.
explanation: Some laptops (Apple silicon, Framework) discharge the battery while plugged in when it is above the configured charge stop threshold. The battery applet's tooltip added 'The power supply is not powerful enough to charge the battery' whenever the system was plugged in and discharging, without looking at the threshold, even though the popup already knew it. Now, when a stop threshold below 100% is set and the battery is at or above it, the tooltip shows the existing 'Battery is configured to charge up to approximately N%.' string instead; otherwise the old message stays.

commits.message:
applets/batterymonitor: don't blame the charger above the charge limit

Some laptops let the battery discharge while plugged in when it is above
its charge limit, and the tooltip then wrongly said the power supply was
too weak. In that case we now show the configured charge limit instead.

BUG: 491731

media.caption: Plugged in, battery at 90% with an 80% charge limit: the tooltip says the power supply is not powerful enough
Same state: the tooltip now says the battery is configured to charge up to approximately 80%

review.text: Clean, focused fix in powerdevil's batterymonitor main.qml: when plugged in and discharging at or above a configured chargeStopThreshold below 100%, toolTipSubText now displays the existing translated charge-limit message from BatteryItem.qml instead of blaming the power supply. Reusing the existing string keeps it translation-safe, the threshold bounds check safely handles unset/invalid values, and the dbusmock UPower + fake KAuth helper verification confirms both the above-threshold fix and below-threshold regression case.

reviews.text: Clean, focused fix in powerdevil's batterymonitor main.qml: when plugged in and discharging at or above a configured chargeStopThreshold below 100%, toolTipSubText now displays the existing translated charge-limit message from BatteryItem.qml instead of blaming the power supply. Reusing the existing string keeps it translation-safe, the threshold bounds check safely handles unset/invalid values, and the dbusmock UPower + fake KAuth helper verification confirms both the above-threshold fix and below-threshold regression case.

Small, correct change in the right place (powerdevil's batterymonitor main.qml): when plugged in and discharging at or above a <100% stop threshold, the tooltip shows the existing charge-limit string instead of blaming the power supply, which is exactly the reporter's expected result. It reuses the same threshold guard as BatteryItem's InhibitionHint and adds no new strings, so it stays cherry-pickable. Before/after screenshots match the captions and the 95%-threshold regression check confirms the old message still appears when the battery is below the limit. The main line still says 'plugged in but still discharging' (reporter suggested 'or similar'), which is acceptable to avoid a new string.
